text.p: Private healthcare group Healthscope Ltd said on Tuesday that its profit after tax for the first four months of the 1996/97 year to June 30 was well below the same period a year earlier.

"Profit after tax for the first four months of the year is substantially below the corresponding period last year, is below budget for this year," chairman Kevin McCann told shareholders at the annual meeting.
"But there has been a material improvement in the performance of the underlying business when compared with the immediately past four months to 30 June 1996," McCann said.

McCann said restoration of profits to acceptable levels depended upon resolution of service issues under its Modbury Hospital contract in Adelaide, improved operating performance of a number of its hospitals, and new business initiatives.
Healthscope did not give any figures for the four months.
The Melbourne-based group reported a net loss of A$4.73 million in the year to June 30, 1996, compared with a profit of A$6.03 million a year earlier.
Healthscope shares ended three cents down at 70 cents.
